The instances to support the device drivers are global such that they are initialized to zero each time the program runs.

detaileddescription.para: They could be local but should at least be static so they are zeroed.

briefdescription.para: The following variable allows a test value to be added to the values that are written to the Flash such that unique values can be generated to guarantee the writes to the Flash were successful.
The following variables hold the data read from and written to the flash and they are global to avoid having large buffers on the stack.

detaileddescription.para: The buffer size accounts for maximum page size and maximum banks - a separate read is performed for each bank, leading to that many (overhead+dummy) bytes.

briefdescription.para: Write buffer.
The following constants specify the max amount of data and the size of the the buffer required to hold the data and overhead to transfer the data to and from the Flash.

detaileddescription.para: Initialized to single flash page size.

briefdescription.para: Writes to the serial Flash connected to the QSPI interface.

detaileddescription.para: All the data put into the buffer must be in the same page of the device with page boundaries being on 256 byte boundaries.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the QSPI driver component to use.
The address to write data to in the Flash.
The number of bytes to write.
The command used to write data to the flash. QSPI device supports only Page Program command to write data to the flash.
Pointer to the write buffer(which is to be transmitted)

briefdescription.para: Reads serial Flash ID connected to the SPI interface.

detaileddescription.para: It then deduces the make and size of the flash and obtains the connection mode to point to corresponding parameters in the flash configuration table. The flash driver functions based on this and it presently supports Micron and Spansion - 128, 256 and 512Mbit and Winbond 128Mbit

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the QSPI driver component to use.
Pointer to the write buffer (which is to be transmitted)
Pointer to the read buffer to which valid received data should be written.

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS if read id, otherwise XST_FAILURE.
